accepted.reason: The bottom margin of page 1 grows by the 2 px (0.51 mm) the Phase A paginator wrongly added after the DANFE's third table (see the danfe pdf-probe entries: Chrome's fourth table at y 232.73, step 233.0, old 235.0). The excess itself (33 mm bottom margin vs the 8 mm maximum) is the 2-page split that both baselines share (DANFE-P1 2 vs 1 page, raw Blitz content 10 px past the page), not this step.
accepted.evidence: DANFE-M1 old 'L 2.498 T 3.429 R 0 B 32.724', new 'L 2.498 T 3.429 R 0 B 33.232' (corpus report); L/T/R unchanged. Box positions: attachments/accepted-evidence.json values.danfeBoxes.
accepted.label: value-compensating-drift

accepted.reason: The worst anchor changes from INV-S1 ('Invoice #: 123', 2.74 mm off in 00-start because the paginator dropped the 8 px UA body margin that Chrome and WeasyPrint both keep) to INV-S4 ('Total: $385.00', 3.09 mm). Every anchor moved by exactly the restored 8 px (2.12 mm): S1 top 27.00 -> 29.12 mm, S4 159.03 -> 161.15 mm. S4 was close to Chrome only because that wrong -8 px offset cancelled raw Blitz's taller table rows (layout-diff N0: 'Total: $385.00' +18 px).
accepted.evidence: corpus/report.json fontCheck boxes (old run copy and this run); Chrome+WeasyPrint baselines of the title from the oracles' word lists: attachments/accepted-evidence.json pdfProbe['oss-sparksuite-invoice'] and values.ossSparksuiteTitle.
accepted.label: value-compensating-drift

accepted.reason:
Pass of 00-start produced by two errors cancelling, not a correct layout. Raw Blitz 0.3.0-beta.4 places the overflow:hidden (BFC) green box beside zero-width floats 200 px too low (flow y 250; Chrome 155 print: 42 = top of its wrapper), and the Phase A paginator ignored both that flow position and the `position: relative; top: -100px` of the second green box (it stacked the two boxes under the

), which happened to draw the 200x200 square. With flow positions kept (relative offsets are honoured, Chrome-verified in tests/pagination_gaps.rs a_relative_offset_on_the_first_block_is_kept_and_may_overlap) both boxes land on Blitz's y 250. The remaining failure is the Blitz float/BFC placement (follow-up), not pagination.
accepted.evidence: Chrome 155 print rects: BFC box y 42 h 100, relative box y 142 h 100 (square 42-242). vellora flow (layout dump): wrapper y 50, BFC box y 250, relative box 350-100 = 250. Old placement: 34 and 134 (stacked, relative offset ignored). New diff region 200x300 at x 8-207, y 50-349. Data: attachments/accepted-evidence.json wpt["css/CSS2/floats/zero-width-floats.html"] (results.json of 00-start and of this run, diff-p1.png measured with Pillow; Chrome 155.0.8059.85 ink data reused from the Phase A beta.4 run, local macOS, INDICATIVE).
accepted.label: wpt-two-errors-cancelling

accepted.reason: False pass of 00-start (WPT reference analysis). The test lays two boxes side by side (an absolutely/relatively positioned stripe next to an in-flow one). The Phase A paginator re-stacked every top-level fragment under the previous one (gap = max(0, flow gap)), so BOTH the test (two block fragments) and the reference (a flattened wrapper whose two inline s became two fragments) were drawn the same wrong way, the second box under the first instead of beside it (for the 3-inch stripes the stacked one leaves no ink in the compared page area: old ink = one stripe, half of Chrome's), and compared equal (maxDifference 0). The step places fragments at their flow positions, so the test now matches Chrome's geometry; what still differs from the reference is a vellora display-list heuristic outside this step: merge_adjacent_rects (RECT_MERGE_TOLERANCE_PX = 4) bridges the real 2-4 px gap between the two background rects of the test, while the reference stripes are images.
accepted.evidence: Old: vellora test == reference (maxDifference 0), ink bbox [8,0,410,225] vs Chrome's test ink [8,19,411,145] (bottom 225 vs 145: stacked, not side by side). New: ink bbox [8,14,410,145] (within 5 px of Chrome's); the only differing pixels are one solid 2x96 px rectangle at x 28-29, y 50-145 (192 px = gap width x stripe height), i.e. exactly the gap between the two stripes that merge_adjacent_rects fills. Data: attachments/accepted-evidence.json wpt["css/CSS2/linebox/line-height-006.xht"] (results.json of 00-start and of this run, diff-p1.png measured with Pillow; Chrome 155.0.8059.85 ink data reused from the Phase A beta.4 run, local macOS, INDICATIVE).

accepted.reason: Old value produced by two errors cancelling, plus one oracle artefact. Descendants of the DANFE's third table overflow its border box by 2 px; the Phase A paginator clamped the resulting negative flow gap to 0 and pushed every later fragment of page 1 down 2 px (1.5 pt). Chrome's continuous flow puts the fourth table at y 232.73, the step at 233.0 (old 235.0): every box after table 3 is 2 px closer to Chrome (layout-diff: old layer P regressed 345 boxes vs the final layer, the new P moves none), and 431 danfe pdf-probe words improve. The 22 listed words were ALREADY above Chrome's position (negative dy: cell-text placement in pre-pagination layers), so removing the spurious +1.5 pt moves them further. The '0,00#k' dx/dy items are an occurrence-pairing artefact of pdf-probe: pdftotext emits the identical '0,00' tokens in a different order after the shift, so the k-th token is paired with a different Chrome token; sorted by position every '0,00' is 1.5 pt CLOSER to Chrome (e.g. 5.26 -> 3.76, 6.03 -> 4.53 pt).

acceptedRegressions.reason: Old value produced by two errors cancelling. These words follow the notification's deadline table, which raw Blitz (layout-diff N0) lays out ~6.5 px lower than Chrome's continuous flow; the Phase A paginator lifted every fragment after it by 6.67 px (it used the previous fragment's 11pt margin-bottom instead of the collapsed 14pt table margin and dropped flow gaps), which put these words near Chrome's by accident (and the signature block 28 px too high). The step keeps the flow gaps (Chrome-verified, tests/pagination_gaps.rs): pagination now adds 0 px on page 1 (layer P == final layer for every run) and the residual +4.02 pt is the raw-Blitz table height, a later step's target.
